content:
The former mayor of Nuevo Laredo may be an international fugitive. Tamaulipas' anti-corruption prosecutor said this week his office is moving to have Interpol issue a red notice for Óscar Enrique Rivas Cuéllar, the PAN politician who ran the border city from 2016 to 2021 — and who, according to the prosecutor, has already left Mexico.

“We are looking for him, and soon we will ask to see if our neighbors to the north help us send him to us as a gift,” said Andrés Norberto García Repper Favila, head of the Fiscalía Especializada en el Combate a la Corrupción, according to La Razón de Tamaulipas — a colorful way of saying the state will ask United States authorities for help locating him.

The announcement follows an October 1 ruling by a federal collegiate court that denied Rivas Cuéllar an amparo against the justified preventive-prison order imposed on him for alleged ejercicio ilícito del servicio público and uso ilícito de atribuciones y facultades — clearing the way for his arrest, according to the reports.

At the center of the case: the 2021 purchase of a parcel of land, reportedly for a convention center, at what prosecutors say was an inflated price — a deal the Fiscalía says cost the municipal treasury more than 50 million pesos. The criminal case, CP 38/2023, sits before a control judge in Nuevo Laredo. Local outlets have put the purchase price at more than 66 million pesos, with the estimated damage to the public purse between 55 and 60 million.

Rivas Cuéllar, one of the first Nuevo Laredo mayors to win reelection to a consecutive term, vanished from public life after the court's ruling. His absence was conspicuous at a PAN gathering photographed October 16 that included Senator Imelda Sanmiguel and other party figures, La Razón noted. Reports in Tamaulipas media say he crossed into the United States — a claim authorities have not officially confirmed.

In the same statement, the anti-corruption chief said Tamaulipas has asked Mexico's Foreign Ministry and the federal Attorney General's Office to move forward with the extradition of former governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca, whose arrest warrant remains active, according to Más Tamaulipas. Rivas Cuéllar has long been described as a political ally of Cabeza de Vaca.

For Laredo, the story lands close to home: if the ex-mayor is indeed on the U.S. side of the river, any handover would run through the same international cooperation channels both countries use every week at the border — and Webb County residents will be watching whether the red notice materializes.

Sources:

  • La Razón de Tamaulipas
  • Más Tamaulipas
  • Op Ciudadana
  • Tamaulipas Habla
  • Subjetivo

— Waldo Wolf, Nuevo Laredo Correspondent, Webb Watch 956

excerpt: Tamaulipas' anti-corruption prosecutor says his office will seek an Interpol red notice for ex-mayor Enrique Rivas Cuellar, who allegedly fled Mexico after losing his bid to block preventive prison in a 50-million-peso land deal case.
title: Tamaulipas Seeks Interpol Red Notice for Ex-Nuevo Laredo Mayor Rivas Cuellar, Says He Fled the Country
